page.title: Lexicon
page.description: The words your firm uses for the product's objects. A term set here replaces the label everywhere the product shows that name on its own — navigation, screen titles, pickers.

accessDenied.title: Workspace managers only
accessDenied.description: The lexicon changes what the whole team reads: it requires the right to manage the team.

language.label: Language of the terms
language.hint: A term is set per language. Some words have no obvious translation, and guessing one would write it wrong.

terms.title: Your team's words
terms.clear: Back to the product's word for “{{concept}}”

version.label: Version {{version}} · last changed on {{date}} by {{who}}
version.unset: Version: not measured yet — the lexicon has never been changed
version.unknownMember: a member no longer on the team

concepts.need: The role a project is looking for
concepts.project: The client project in the pipe
concepts.consultant: The person your firm puts forward
concepts.submission: A consultant put forward on a need

forbidden.title: Words never to read
forbidden.hint: {{copilot}} stops using them in anything she drafts. And if a forbidden word is the product's own, you must also say what replaces it — otherwise it would stay on screen.
forbidden.placeholder: e.g. the word you no longer want to read

outOfScope.title: What the lexicon does not change
outOfScope.hint: A lexicon that states what it does not do beats one that lies about half of it.

items.sentences: Sentences. “No account matches” keeps its word: agreeing it would need a grammar, and skipping that would write nonsense.
items.document_titles: The browser tab title, which composes the product name with the screen name.
items.third_party_objects: The objects of a connected tool, on that connector's own screens — renaming them would misstate what the tool reads.
items.pricing_grid: The pricing grid: it is shared by every workspace.
items.cross_workspace_metrics: Metrics comparable across workspaces — renaming them would break the comparison.

violations.preferred_is_forbidden: “{{term}}” is both the word you prefer and a word you forbid.
violations.forbidden_without_replacement: You forbid “{{term}}”, which is the product's own word: give the term to use instead, otherwise it stays on screen.
